![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14216822/assets/08ee9a92a96f2ab0e4644dc02dfd4be605e72e9b778f54bf60d8e4014d58a7bd.png)

Given that the point $A$ has coordinates $(-3\sqrt{3},9)$, calculate the angle $\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
We can form a triangle by creating a vertical line from $A$ to the $x$-axis. Let us call ${\theta }^{′}$ the acute angle that is supplementary to $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14216822/assets/e0643cdb2d864b3af6466e24ab815dc8085e811dfdb86cdce253981a521faf82.png)

Using the tangent ratio, we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{\theta }^{′}=\frac{9}{3\sqrt{3}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}.
$$

Finally, using the inverse tangent, we get

$$
{\theta }^{′}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Since $\theta +{\theta }^{′}=\pi ,$ then $\theta =\pi -{\theta }^{′}=\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$
